rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence is entirely absent, so the first experiment should establish a baseline by testing the simplest configuration (rna_only with singleprofile and pca_n2000). This clarifies the baseline performance of RNA-only models and isolates the impact of the rna_encoder and profile_setting. It directly addresses the importance of modality and encoding choices, which are critical design decisions.

The existing evidence shows that RNA-only singleprofile with PCA achieves 0.4849 accuracy. This experiment tests multiprofile with avgpool aggregation, isolating the impact of profile setting and aggregation. It directly addresses uncertainty about whether multi-profile data or aggregation methods improve performance, balancing exploration of key design choices without overcomplicating the model.

Existing evidence shows that multiprofile (config_002) outperforms singleprofile (config_001) for RNA-only models. This experiment tests whether switching the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 (config_002) to scvi_n200 while maintaining multiprofile and avgpool aggregation isolates the impact of encoder choice. It directly compares two RNA encoders (pca vs scvi) under the same profile and aggregation settings, which are already shown to be beneficial. This clarifies whether encoder complexity matters, avoiding simultaneous changes to multiple factors.

Existing evidence shows that RNA-only multiprofile with scvi_n200 (config_005) achieves the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests adding image data (multimodal) with the same RNA encoder and profile setting to isolate the effect of image integration, a critical design choice. It balances exploitation of the current strong RNA-only setup with exploration of multimodal potential.

Existing evidence shows that RNA-only models with multiprofile and scvi_n200 encoder (config_005) achieve the highest accuracy (0.650). This experiment tests whether replacing avgpool aggregation (used in config_005) with transformer aggregation improves performance, isolating the effect of aggregation method. It balances exploitation of the strong RNA-only baseline with exploration of a key design choice, avoiding unnecessary complexity while addressing a critical uncertainty.

Existing evidence shows RNA-only models with scvi_n200 encoder and transformer aggregation (config_006) achieve the highest accuracy (0.652970). This experiment tests whether combining this RNA setup with image data (resnet50) via multimodal concat fusion can improve performance. It directly addresses whether multimodal integration enhances results, a critical design choice with sparse evidence. This balances exploitation of the current RNA-only success with exploration of multimodal potential.

Existing evidence shows that transformer aggregation (config_006: 0.652970, config_032: 0.687833) and scvi_n200 RNA encoder (config_005: 0.650124, config_032: 0.687833) are effective. This experiment tests scgpt RNA encoder with transformer aggregation (config_044) to isolate the impact of RNA representation while maintaining the effective aggregation method. It directly compares scgpt vs scvi_n200 under the same transformer aggregation and concat fusion setup, addressing uncertainty about RNA encoder choice without changing multiple factors.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder, resnet50 image encoder, and transformer aggregation achieve high performance (config_032: 0.6878 accuracy). This experiment tests whether changing fusion from concat to weighted improves performance, isolating the effect of fusion method. It builds on the strong foundation of config_032 while exploring a critical design choice with minimal parameter changes.

Existing evidence shows that weighted fusion and transformer aggregation significantly improve performance (config_033: 0.713 accuracy). This experiment tests whether using the more advanced imagenet_vit_l image encoder (vs. resnet50) with the same RNA encoder (scvi_n200), aggregation (transformer), and fusion (weighted) could further improve performance. It isolates the effect of the image encoder while maintaining the proven effective components, addressing uncertainty about whether image encoder choice is critical for multimodal success.

Existing evidence shows that using imagenet_vit_l as the image encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion achieve high performance (config_039: 0.7249 accuracy). This experiment tests whether replacing the RNA encoder from scvi_n200 to scgpt (a more complex model) maintains or improves performance, isolating the impact of RNA encoder choice. It balances exploitation of proven components with exploration of a key design decision.
